text: Rust allows only one mutable reference at a time so that mutation is exclusive and no other alias can read or write the same value while it changes. That rule blocks data races and the wider class of memory-safety bugs from aliased mutation, including iterator invalidation and use-after-free.
thought:
The user is asking about Rust's borrow checker: why it forbids two mutable references to the same value, and what bug class that prevents.

Rust enforces exclusive mutable access to prevent data races and undefined behavior from aliased mutation.

The rule applies even in single-threaded code. It prevents iterator invalidation, use-after-free, and memory corruption from simultaneous mutation through aliases.
